Keep Calgary-Klein's boundaries as they are, including Mayland Heights and Tuxedo Park.

Keep seats within cities where possible, allotting seats by population: Calgary 28, Edmonton 21, Red Deer 2, Lethbridge 2, and one city seat plus one hybrid for Grande Prairie, Medicine Hat, Airdrie and St. Albert.

quote: Airdrie, again, would continue to have one seat and one hybrid seat
note: Asks that Airdrie continue with one seat and one hybrid (the in-force Airdrie-East and Airdrie-Cochrane pattern), defending Airdrie-Cochrane as a community of interest; boundaries not specified, hence direction. Rejection of A2 from his answer to a commissioner (EB-199): 'So if you have a hybrid Airdrie-Calgary riding, how then do you manage those competing interests?' and 'within Airdrie and the rural context, the economic development factors are different than they would be for Calgary'.

quote: So they created AirdrieCochrane. I think there’s a community of interest because they’re both satellite communities outside of Calgary.
note: Describes Airdrie-Cochrane as having a community of interest but calls hybrids 'the least bad option' and asks nothing about Cochrane's own district; left without a want (rule 17). A second reader might code C4 direction.

quote: Calgary, 28 seats; Edmonton, 21 seats; Red Deer, two seats; Lethbridge, two seats; Medicine Hat, one seat and one hybrid seat
note: Seat allocation by population, under the principle 'where possible, keep seats contained within cities'; Red Deer's two seats are listed apart from the 'hybrid' seats given to other cities, so read as two seats within the city.

quote: Calgary, 28 seats; Edmonton, 21 seats; Red Deer, two seats; Lethbridge, two seats; Medicine Hat, one seat and one hybrid seat
note: Same seat list as REDDEER; Lethbridge's two seats are listed apart from hybrid seats, under the principle of keeping seats within cities.

quote: Airdrie, again, would continue to have one seat and one hybrid seat; St. Albert would have one seat and one hybrid seat
note: One St. Albert city seat and one hybrid: the long-standing pattern, nothing more said.

asks: Hold population variances to about plus or minus 10 per cent (5 per cent in cities), publish each division's area and density, allow for eligible-voter differences and growth, and let the commission recommend the number of seats.

quote: If you’re in a Chestermere or you’re in an Airdrie or a Cochrane, I would submit that you’re not too far different than what you are as a Calgarian
note: Answering a commissioner on hybrids: says the first ring of satellite towns is much like Calgary and 'If you want to call that a hybrid, I think that makes sense to me', while hybrids reaching further into rural areas are less apt. An opinion on what hybrids are acceptable, not a request for any Airdrie arrangement; left without a want (rule 17). Also refers to the current Airdrie split as a hybrid.

quote: If you’re in a Chestermere or you’re in an Airdrie or a Cochrane, I would submit that you’re not too far different than what you are as a Calgarian
note: Same passage as AIRDRIE: says a Calgary-plus-first-ring hybrid 'makes sense to me', but makes no request for Cochrane; no want (rule 17).

quote: If you’re in a Chestermere or you’re in an Airdrie or a Cochrane, I would submit that you’re not too far different than what you are as a Calgarian
note: Same passage as AIRDRIE: an opinion that such a hybrid makes sense, not a request about Chestermere; no want (rule 17). A second reader might code H2 direction.

asks: Avoid urban-rural split ridings except where necessary, keep like communities together, and leave Calgary-Klein exactly as it is.

quote: So I would say that Airdrie has different interests from Calgary and different interests from truly rural communities.
note: In answer to a commissioner's question on north Calgary and Airdrie; also says the north edge of Calgary 'would be closer in interest to Airdrie'. No request or explicit rejection about how Airdrie is divided; her general ask is to avoid urban-rural hybrids except where necessary.

asks: Keep communities whole and like with like: put all three Stoney Nakoda communities (adding Eden Valley and Bighorn) in Banff-Kananaskis, unite Millarville in one riding, keep the MD of Bighorn with Banff and Canmore, keep Banff-Kananaskis a foothills-mountain riding without Cochrane, Airdrie or parts of Calgary, and extend it along the eastern slopes if it must change.

quote: I would just say: please don’t put us with Cochrane or Airdrie.
note: Banff-Kananaskis MLA (Canmore resident) asks that the Bow Valley not be joined again with Cochrane, recalling the former Banff-Cochrane riding. A rejection only; nothing asked for Cochrane's own district.
Airdrie named only in 'please don't put us with Cochrane or Airdrie'; nothing about how Airdrie is divided.

quote: One of my recommendations would be to include Eden Valley and Bighorn in the riding of Banff-Kananaskis, just to make sure that all of the Stoney Nation communities are in one riding.
note: Notes the Bighorn Stoney reserve 'is currently in the Rimbey-Rocky Mountain House riding' and asks it be moved to Banff-Kananaskis with the other Stoney communities; also wants the MD of Bighorn kept with Banff and Canmore ('they have a lot more in common with Banff and Canmore', EB-204). Bow Valley district apart from Rocky Mountain House, hence B2 direction. Answering a commissioner, she also finds Banff with Jasper workable issue-wise (CANMORE-JASPER, not coded here).
Rimbey-Rocky Mountain House riding named only as where the Bighorn reserve now sits; no request about the west-central riding itself.
Red Deer named only in an aside on how the word 'rural' is used.
Lethbridge named only in an aside on how the word 'rural' is used.

asks: Split Cochrane from Airdrie and form a new riding around Cochrane, taking in Bearspaw and nearby acreages, and give Airdrie two representatives of its own.

quote: I believe that Cochrane needs to be split from the Airdrie riding and a new riding formulated around Cochrane.
note: Former Cochrane councillor. Suggests picking up population from Bearspaw ('our schools draw from the Bearspaw area') and, answering a commissioner, includes Cochrane Lake and MonTerra; calls Springbank 'another world'. Rejection quote: 'the concept of a hybrid that we are currently in in Airdrie-Cochrane is not fair to either Airdrie or Cochrane'. The record carries no EB label, so the page is its PDF range.

quote: I think that the people of Airdrie would find that having two representatives – and I think they could meet the threshold for two – would be advisable
note: Wants two Airdrie-centred seats instead of Airdrie-Cochrane; does not say whether they take in rural Rocky View (A1) or are Airdrie-only (A3), so A1 at direction; a second reader might choose A3.
